title: Siegfried acquires Luxembourg castle
description: Count Siegfried obtains the rock of Lucilinburhuc by exchange with an abbey in Trier, the start of the town and the county.

title: Henry VII elected King of the Romans
description: The count of Luxembourg is chosen to rule the Holy Roman Empire, the first of four emperors from his house.

title: Luxembourg raised to a duchy
description: Emperor Charles IV makes the county a duchy for his half-brother Wenceslaus.

title: Burgundian conquest
description: Philip the Good of Burgundy takes the city by surprise, and the duchy becomes part of the Burgundian and later Habsburg Netherlands.

title: Siege of Luxembourg
description: A French army under Vauban takes the fortress, which Vauban then rebuilds into one of the strongest in Europe.

title: Fortress surrenders to the French Republic
description: After a siege of seven months the Austrian garrison gives up, and Luxembourg is annexed to France as the Forêts department.

title: Grand Duchy created
description: The Congress of Vienna makes Luxembourg a grand duchy under the king of the Netherlands, in the German Confederation, with a Prussian garrison.

title: Third partition of Luxembourg
description: The Treaty of London gives the French-speaking western half to Belgium and leaves the grand duchy with its present borders.

title: Luxembourg joins the Zollverein
description: Entry into the German customs union ties the economy to Germany and later feeds the steel industry.

title: Second Treaty of London
description: After France tries to buy the grand duchy, the powers declare it neutral for ever, and the Prussian garrison leaves and the fortress is pulled down.

title: Constitution of 1868
description: The constitution that, much amended, is still in force restores parliamentary government.

title: End of the union with the Netherlands
description: William III dies without a son, and under the Nassau family pact the grand duchy passes to Adolphe of Nassau-Weilburg and gets its own dynasty.

title: ARBED founded
description: Three firms merge into the steel company that dominates the economy for most of the century.

title: German occupation of 1914
description: German troops occupy the neutral grand duchy on the way to France and stay for four years.

title: Referendum of 1919
description: Voters choose to keep the monarchy under Grand Duchess Charlotte and prefer an economic union with France.

title: Economic union with Belgium
description: After France declines, Luxembourg signs a customs and currency union with Belgium.

title: German invasion of 1940
description: Germany overruns the country in a day; the grand duchess and the government go into exile, and Luxembourg is later annexed to the Reich.

title: General strike of 1942
description: Workers strike against conscription into the German army; 21 strikers are shot.

title: Liberation
description: American troops enter the capital, with Prince Félix and Hereditary Grand Duke Jean among them.

title: Seat of the Coal and Steel Community
description: The High Authority of the European Coal and Steel Community starts work in Luxembourg, making the city one of the capitals of European integration.

title: Schengen Agreement
description: On a boat on the Moselle, five states agree to do away with checks at their shared borders.

title: Grand Duke Jean abdicates
description: Jean hands the throne to his son Henri after a reign of 36 years.
